title: Beyond the First Footsteps
title_ja: 最初の一歩の向こうにあるもの
fact_notes: アポロ11号打ち上げ1969年7月16日
1961年ケネディ大統領の目標表明
月面の船外活動約2時間半

sentences.en: On July 20, 1969, two astronauts walked on the Moon while a third remained in orbit, creating a moment that many people still remember today.
sentences.ja: 1969年7月20日、2人の宇宙飛行士が月面を歩き、3人目は軌道上に残りました。この瞬間は今も多くの人の記憶に残っています。

sentences.en: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin explored the lunar surface, while Michael Collins operated the command module that would help bring the crew home.
sentences.ja: ニール・アームストロングとバズ・オルドリンは月面を探査し、マイケル・コリンズは乗組員の帰還を支える司令船を操作しました。

sentences.en: Their achievement is often presented as a story of individual courage, but that description leaves out an important part of the mission.
sentences.ja: 彼らの功績は個人の勇気の物語として紹介されがちですが、その説明では任務の重要な一面が抜け落ちています。

sentences.en: The flight also depended on thousands of workers who had planned, tested, and checked different pieces of a complicated technological system.
sentences.ja: その飛行は、複雑な技術体系のさまざまな部分を計画し、試験し、点検した何千人もの人々にも支えられていました。

sentences.en: Understanding Apollo 11 therefore requires us to consider not only the astronauts but also the organization that made their journey possible.
sentences.ja: したがって、アポロ11号を理解するには宇宙飛行士だけでなく、旅を可能にした組織についても考える必要があります。

sentences.en: The mission began on July 16, 1969, when Apollo 11 launched toward the Moon carrying Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins.
sentences.ja: その任務は1969年7月16日、アームストロング、オルドリン、コリンズを乗せたアポロ11号が月に向けて打ち上げられた時に始まりました。

sentences.en: The goal was connected to a challenge announced by President John F. Kennedy in 1961: landing humans on the Moon and returning them safely to Earth.
sentences.ja: 目標は1961年にジョン・F・ケネディ大統領が示した、人間を月に着陸させ無事に地球へ帰還させるという挑戦につながっていました。

sentences.en: Reaching the lunar surface was only one part of this plan, because a successful landing would mean little without a safe return.
sentences.ja: 月面到達は計画の一部分にすぎず、無事に帰還できなければ着陸の成功はほとんど意味を持たないからです。

sentences.en: Engineers had to think about navigation, communication, fuel, and the difficult task of connecting spacecraft after the lunar exploration.
sentences.ja: 技術者たちは航法、通信、燃料、そして月面探査後に宇宙船を再び接続する難しい作業を考えなければなりませんでした。

sentences.en: In this sense, Apollo 11 was not a single dramatic event but a long sequence of decisions in which mistakes could have serious consequences.
sentences.ja: この意味でアポロ11号は一つの劇的な出来事ではなく、誤りが重大な結果をもたらし得る長い意思決定の連続でした。

sentences.en: On the Moon, Armstrong and Aldrin collected samples and placed scientific instruments, allowing researchers to study a world far from Earth.
sentences.ja: 月ではアームストロングとオルドリンが試料を採取し科学機器を設置して、研究者が地球から遠く離れた世界を調べられるようにしました。

sentences.en: NASA records that the two astronauts spent about two and a half hours outside their lunar module during the surface exploration.
sentences.ja: NASAの記録によれば、2人は月面探査中に月着陸船の外で約2時間半を過ごしました。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Collins continued to travel around the Moon, preparing for the moment when the separated parts of the spacecraft would meet again.
sentences.ja: その間、コリンズは月の周りを飛行し続け、分離した宇宙船の部分が再会する時に備えていました。

sentences.en: The photographs of the first footsteps are famous, yet the less visible work of measurement and coordination was equally necessary.
sentences.ja: 最初の足跡の写真は有名ですが、目に見えにくい測定や調整の作業も同じくらい必要でした。

sentences.en: This contrast reminds us that public attention often goes to spectacular results rather than to the careful processes behind them.
sentences.ja: この対比は、人々の注目が結果の背後にある慎重な過程よりも、目を引く成果に集まりがちだと気づかせます。

sentences.en: Apollo 11 returned to Earth on July 24, 1969, completing the journey and demonstrating that human travel to another celestial body was possible.
sentences.ja: アポロ11号は1969年7月24日に地球へ帰還し、旅を完了して人類が別の天体へ移動できることを示しました。

sentences.en: However, one successful mission did not mean that space exploration had suddenly become easy, inexpensive, or free from danger.
sentences.ja: しかし、一度の任務の成功は、宇宙探査が突然簡単で安価で危険のないものになったことを意味しません。

sentences.en: Future projects would still require difficult choices about money, technology, scientific priorities, and the level of risk society was willing to accept.
sentences.ja: 将来の計画にも、費用、技術、科学的優先事項、社会が受け入れるリスクの水準について難しい選択が必要となるでしょう。

sentences.en: A project may be scientifically valuable while still raising a reasonable question about how public resources should be used.
sentences.ja: ある計画は科学的に価値があっても、公的資源をどう使うべきかというもっともな疑問を提起する場合があります。

sentences.en: Rather than treating these questions as signs of opposition to science, we can regard them as part of responsible decision making.
sentences.ja: こうした疑問を科学への反対の表れとみなすのではなく、責任ある意思決定の一部として考えることができます。

sentences.en: Today, Apollo 11 offers a useful example of how ambitious goals can bring together knowledge from many specialized fields.
sentences.ja: 今日、アポロ11号は野心的な目標が多くの専門分野の知識を結びつける仕組みを示す有用な例となっています。

sentences.en: Its history also encourages a more careful definition of success, one that includes safe operations, scientific learning, and cooperation among workers.
sentences.ja: その歴史は、安全な運用、科学的学習、作業者同士の協力を含む、より慎重な成功の定義を促します。

sentences.en: The famous moment on the lunar surface was the visible result of years of preparation, and it should not be separated from that preparation.
sentences.ja: 月面での有名な瞬間は何年もの準備の目に見える結果であり、その準備と切り離してはいけません。

sentences.en: For students considering future technologies, this perspective may be more useful than simply memorizing the names and dates of the mission.
sentences.ja: 未来の技術を考える生徒にとって、この視点は任務の名前や日付を覚えるだけよりも役立つかもしれません。

sentences.en: It invites them to ask how people can pursue difficult goals without forgetting the responsibility that comes with powerful tools.
sentences.ja: それは強力な道具に伴う責任を忘れずに、人々が難しい目標を追求するにはどうすればよいかと問いかけます。

questions.prompt: What is the writer's main purpose?
options: To argue that Apollo 11 accomplished very little
To show that space projects should never use public money
To explain why Apollo 11 was a collective achievement requiring responsible choices
To describe every technical part of the spacecraft
questions.explanation_ja: 宇宙飛行士の偉業から、集団的な準備と責任ある意思決定に焦点を広げています。

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, why was a safe return essential?
options: The mission objective included returning the astronauts to Earth.
The astronauts had no scientific work on the Moon.
The journey was originally planned as a one-way trip.
Collins was not involved in the return flight.
questions.explanation_ja: a successful landing would mean little without a safe return が、returning astronauts was part of the objective に言い換えられています。

questions.prompt: 'the less visible work' in paragraph 3 most nearly refers to ____.
options: the public celebration of the mission
measurement and coordination that received less attention
the photographs taken on the Moon
the first human footprints
questions.explanation_ja: the less visible work を直後の measurement and coordination が具体化しています。

questions.prompt: How does the writer view questions about the cost of space exploration?
options: As evidence that science is worthless
As inappropriate in democratic discussions
As a legitimate part of making responsible decisions
As less important than public excitement
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落では資源配分への疑問も responsible decision making の一部と捉えます。

questions.prompt: What does 'However' at the start of paragraph 4 introduce?
options: A contrast between a successful mission and continued challenges
A definition of a lunar module
An additional fact about the crew's names
A reason why the launch date changed
questions.explanation_ja: 成功後も費用や危険の問題が残るという逆接を示します。

questions.prompt: Which description best matches the structure of the passage?
options: Personal story → unrelated statistics → travel advice
Achievement → mission requirements → behind-the-scenes work → policy questions → wider lesson
Scientific experiment → medical history → legal argument
A list of astronauts without any argument
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の問題提起から第5段落の一般化への展開を把握する設問です。

whileは譲歩的対比。科学的価値があることと資源配分の問題が共存します。
